title: My day
topic: pronominal verbs in the present; telling the time
why: Unit 2 starts with your day: the pronominal verbs of daily routine (se lever, se doucher, s'habiller…) and telling the time, from et quart to the 24-hour clock. You can now describe your typical day, from breakfast to bedtime.

{"lessons": ["

Verbs with me, te, se

Many verbs of daily routine are pronominal in French: they come with an extra pronoun that refers back to the subject. Je me lave is literally “I wash myself”. English usually drops the “myself”: “I get up”, “I shower”, “I get dressed”. French never drops it.

se réveiller (to wake up)s'habiller (to get dressed)
jeje me réveilleje m'habille
tutu te réveillestu t'habilles
il, elle, onil se réveilleelle s'habille
nousnous nous réveillonsnous nous habillons
vousvous vous réveillezvous vous habillez
ils, ellesils se réveillentelles s'habillent

The endings are those of the -er verbs you know. Only the pronoun is new: me, te, se, nous, vous, se. Before a vowel or a silent h, me, te, se become m', t', s'. Yes, nous nous and vous vous are normal!

S'appeler, explained at last

Je m'appelle is a pronominal verb: “I call myself”. Note the spelling: two l's when the ending is silent (je m'appelle, tu t'appelles, ils s'appellent), one l with nous and vous (nous nous appelons, vous vous appelez). Se lever works the same way with an accent: je me lève, ils se lèvent, but nous nous levons.

The negative

Ne goes before the pronoun, pas after the verb: the pronoun stays glued to its verb.

Je ne me lève pas tôt le dimanche.I don't get up early on Sundays.
Tu ne te reposes pas ?Aren't you resting?

Some verbs change meaning without the pronoun: je lave la voiture (I wash the car) / je me lave (I wash, myself). Je couche alone is not what you want: say je me couche (I go to bed).

", "

Quelle heure est-il ?

To ask the time, say Quelle heure est-il ? (a fixed inverted phrase) or, more casually, Il est quelle heure ? The answer always starts with il est and always includes the word heure(s), which English often leaves out (“it's eight” → il est huit heures).

timeFrenchnote
1:00Il est une heure.singular, feminine: une heure
8:00Il est huit heures.
8:10Il est huit heures dix.minutes after the hour
8:15Il est huit heures et quart.
8:30Il est huit heures et demie.demie with -e
8:45Il est neuf heures moins le quart.nine minus a quarter
8:50Il est neuf heures moins dix.nine minus ten
12:00Il est midi. / Il est minuit.noon / midnight: no heures

“At” a time is à: à huit heures, à midi. To avoid confusion, you can add du matin (in the morning), de l'après-midi (in the afternoon) or du soir (in the evening): à sept heures du soir.

The 24-hour clock

Timetables, shops, trains and appointments use the 24-hour clock, and the French say it aloud too: 20 h 30 = vingt heures trente. In this system, you never use et quart, et demie or moins: 18 h 45 is dix-huit heures quarante-cinq.

Le train arrive à 18 h 15.The train arrives at 6:15 p.m. (dix-huit heures quinze)

In writing, the French use h, not a colon: 8 h 30, 20 h. And there's no “a.m.” or “p.m.”.

", "

Meals and a French day

French meals have fixed names and fairly fixed times. Careful: the words don't match English one to one.

mealEnglishusual time
le petit-déjeunerbreakfast7 h – 8 h
le déjeunerlunch12 h – 13 h 30
le goûterafternoon snack (for children)16 h 30
le dînerdinner19 h 30 – 20 h 30

Déjeuner and dîner are also regular -er verbs: je déjeune à midi, nous dînons à vingt heures. In Belgium, Switzerland and Quebec, le déjeuner is breakfast and le dîner is lunch (dinner is le souper): useful to know, but in France, stick to the table above.

A typical day

Je me réveille à sept heures. Je me lève, je me douche et je m'habille.I wake up at seven. I get up, I shower and I get dressed.
Je déjeune à midi et demi avec des collègues.I have lunch at twelve thirty with colleagues.
Le soir, je dîne à vingt heures, je me repose et je me couche à minuit.In the evening, I have dinner at eight, I relax and I go to bed at midnight.

Notice midi et demi, without an -e: midi is masculine, unlike heure. And when you're late: Je me dépêche ! (I'm hurrying!)

le matin, le soir with le mean “in the morning”, “in the evening” in general, like le samedi for “on Saturdays”.
